package.title: Open enrollment: 5 questions to ask about tirzepatide or semaglutide coverage for 2027 (US)

social.instagram_caption:
Open enrollment is open — is tirzepatide or semaglutide actually covered on your 2027 plan? 📋

Coverage for GLP-1 medicines keeps shifting: Walmart told reporters (Oct 13, 2026) that in 2027, employees with type 2 diabetes can get some GLP-1s at $0 with a new prior authorization, while an employer survey found some companies plan to drop coverage for weight loss in 2027. The only way to know your plan is to ask.

5 questions to bring to open enrollment:
→ Covered for diabetes, weight, or both? (Same medicine, different brand names, different approved uses)
→ Is prior authorization required — and what documents does your prescriber need to send?
→ Is step therapy required (try another drug first)?
→ What's your actual cost — tier, copay/coinsurance, deductible, pharmacy rules?
→ Does a savings card even apply to your plan? (Many exclude Medicare/Medicaid. On Medicare? CMS has extended its GLP-1 Bridge program through Dec 31, 2027, as of Oct 2026; ask Medicare or your plan if you qualify.)

Save this before you pick a plan, and share it with someone who's navigating open enrollment too.

If your coverage changes: only use a licensed pharmacy with a valid prescription, skip unapproved, compounded or gray-market copies (FDA has flagged concerns), and don't stop or change your medicine without talking to your prescriber first.

factcheck.summary: The carousel is accurate and safe. I checked the key numbers and sources. KFF 2025 says "19% of firms with 200 or more workers, including 43% of firms with 5,000 or more workers, cover GLP-1 drugs for weight loss in their largest health plan." The page breaks that down as 16%, 30% and 43% by firm size. The HealthCare.gov preauthorization glossary exists. The FDA page on unapproved GLP-1 drugs exists, is "content current as of Oct 1, 2026", and backs the licensed-pharmacy line and the warning about compounded products. Manufacturer coupons can't be used with Medicare or other government plans. The safety checklist is good: licensed pharmacy, no gray-market products, no stopping without the prescriber. The CTA has the disclaimer and the full prescriber line. No dosing, no sellers. All issues are minor wording and completeness fixes: tighten the preauthorization paraphrase, add 'largest plan' to the chart, add the Medicare 2027 status line given the 2027 framing, mention other approved uses on Q1, and replace the FDA URL with the canonical one it redirects to.

issues.claim: Prior authorization means your plan has to approve a drug before it pays for it (HealthCare.gov).
issues.problem: This overstates the source. HealthCare.gov defines preauthorization as the plan's decision that a drug is medically necessary, and says preauthorization isn't a promise the plan will cover the cost. As written, it suggests approval means the plan pays.
issues.fix: Prior authorization means your plan must decide a drug is medically necessary before covering it, and approval isn't a promise it will pay (HealthCare.gov). Ask about each step below.

issues.claim: KFF 2025 Employer Health Benefits Survey, firms that offer health benefits.
issues.problem: KFF's figures are for coverage in each firm's largest health plan in 2025. They're also 2025 data shown in a carousel about 2027 coverage.
issues.fix: KFF 2025 Employer Health Benefits Survey: firms that offer health benefits, coverage in their largest plan in 2025. Weight loss only; diabetes coverage is a separate question. 2027 plans may differ.

issues.claim: Official manufacturer savings programs often exclude government plans like Medicare and Medicaid.
issues.problem: This is accurate, but the carousel is framed around 2027 and leaves out Medicare's current status. CMS has extended the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge (fixed $50 copay for some weight-management GLP-1s, outside Part D, no coupons) through Dec 31, 2027, and the Part D BALANCE Model won't start in 2027. Medicare viewers would be left without the main option relevant to them.
issues.fix: Q5: Official manufacturer savings programs often exclude government plans like Medicare and Medicaid. On Medicare? CMS has extended its GLP-1 Bridge program through Dec 31, 2027 (as of Oct 2026); ask Medicare or your plan if you qualify. Read each program's terms, and ask your pharmacist whether it applies to your plan.

issues.claim: Wegovy / Zepbound listed only under 'Weight management'
issues.problem: Wegovy is also approved to lower heart attack and stroke risk in adults with heart disease and overweight/obesity, and for MASH. Zepbound is also approved for moderate-to-severe sleep apnea in adults with obesity. Plans, including Medicare, may cover them for those uses, which is part of the coverage question Q1 asks.
issues.fix: Change the body to: "The same medicine is sold under different brand names for different approved uses (Wegovy and Zepbound also have some approved uses beyond weight). A plan can cover one use and not another."

issues.claim: Do you pay full price first?
issues.problem: Before the deductible is met, you usually pay the plan's negotiated price, not the list price. 'Full price' could be read as list price.
issues.fix: Do you pay the plan's full negotiated price until you meet it?

issues.problem: The URL 301-redirects to a new canonical path, and the page is dated 'content current as of Oct 1, 2026'.
issues.fix: url: https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-alerts-and-statements/fdas-concerns-unapproved-glp-1-drugs-used-weight-loss ; year: 2026 (content current as of Oct 1, 2026)
